record.original_question: How can effective theories written in observable hadron degrees of freedom be rigorously justified as low-energy limits of QCD rather than treated as phenomenological models whose connection to the underlying quark-and-gluon theory remains unproven?

evidence.quote: Approaches to nonperturbative description of QCD may be divided into two classes: (1) calculations in QCD beyond the perturbation theory (the only available method here is the numerical calculation of the functional integral on the lattice) and (2) construction of an effective theory in terms of degrees of freedom which correspond to obsevrable particles.
In the latter case the main unsolved question is, as a rule, to justify the connection of the effective theory to QCD.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) is the non-Abelian gauge theory with gauge group SU(3) whose elementary fields are quarks (Dirac fermions in the fundamental representation) and gluons (gauge bosons in the adjoint representation), defined by the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\text{QCD}} = -\tfrac{1}{4} G^{a}_{\mu\nu} G^{a\,\mu\nu} + \sum_f \bar{\psi}_f (i\gamma^\mu D_\mu - m_f)\psi_f$, where $G^{a}_{\mu\nu}$ is the gluon field strength and $D_\mu$ is the gauge-covariant derivative. At low energies ($E \lesssim 1$ GeV), QCD is strongly coupled and color confinement renders quarks and gluons unobservable as asymptotic states; the observed asymptotic states are color-singlet hadrons (mesons, baryons, glueballs).

Various effective theories are written directly in terms of hadronic degrees of freedom (e.g., chiral perturbation theory built from pseudo-Goldstone meson fields, heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory, nucleon–meson Lagrangians, vector meson dominance models, Skyrme-type soliton models, etc.), each with its own Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\text{eff}}[\phi_{\text{had}}]$ and a power-counting expansion in momenta and quark masses.

Problem. Provide a mathematically rigorous derivation, starting from the QCD generating functional
$$Z_{\text{QCD}}[J] = \int \mathcal{D}A\,\mathcal{D}\psi\,\mathcal{D}\bar\psi\; e^{i S_{\text{QCD}}[A,\psi,\bar\psi] + i\int J\cdot \mathcal{O}}\,,$$
of an effective hadronic action $S_{\text{eff}}[\phi_{\text{had}}]$ such that the low-energy Green functions of suitable composite QCD operators $\mathcal{O}(x)$ (interpolating fields for hadrons) coincide, order by order in a controlled low-energy expansion, with those computed from $S_{\text{eff}}$, with all coefficients (low-energy constants) determined as explicit functionals of QCD. Equivalently, establish a rigorous mapping between QCD and an effective hadronic theory that justifies the latter as the genuine low-energy limit of QCD, rather than as a phenomenological ansatz with parameters fitted to data.
artifact.status_search_result: The rigorous derivation of hadronic effective theories from QCD remains an open problem. While chiral perturbation theory and other effective frameworks are well established phenomenologically, and partial nonperturbative connections (large-$N_c$ expansion, lattice QCD determinations of low-energy constants, Seiberg-like dualities in supersymmetric cousins) provide supporting evidence, no rigorous derivation of a hadronic effective Lagrangian from the QCD path integral exists. This is closely tied to the Yang–Mills mass gap problem, one of the Clay Millennium Prize Problems, which is also unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Yang–Mills and Mass Gap
status_evidence.snippet: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap. ... This problem remains unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: The rigorous nonperturbative construction of QCD-like Yang–Mills theory remains an open Millennium Problem, indicating that a rigorous derivation of low-energy effective hadronic theories from QCD is also unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Perturbation Theory (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Chiral perturbation theory is the effective field theory of QCD at low energies; its low-energy constants must currently be determined from experiment or lattice QCD.
status_evidence.claim: Standard hadronic effective theories rely on matching coefficients to data or lattice computations rather than a rigorous derivation from QCD.
